newsitem.title: USA: California Senate paves way for state tobacco suit.
newsitem.headline: California Senate paves way for state tobacco suit.

text.p: California's Senate on Thursday approved a bill to eliminate the special immunity from product liability lawsuits enjoyed by tobacco products in the state.

The state Senate approved the bill, by Senator Quentin Kopp, on a vote of 28-to-9, his office said. The bill now advances to the Assembly Judiciary Committee, where it could be taken up in the coming weeks.

If passed by the Assembly and signed by Gov. Pete Wilson, Kopp's bill would remove an obstacle preventing Republican state Attorney General Dan Lungren from filing a state lawsuit against the tobacco companies, lawmakers said.

The current immunity for tobacco products was part of 1987 legislation intended to curtail the number of product liability lawsuits by granting immunity to the manufacturers of certain products. In addition to tobacco, other consumer products, including sugar, castor oil, alcohol and butter, were included in the immunity legislation.
